examples.claim: Introl-cited benchmarks: TensorRT-LLM highest performance despite complex setup
examples.source: Introl: 'TensorRT-LLM delivers maximum performance on NVIDIA hardware ... The tradeoff: complex setup requiring checkpoint conversion, engine building'
blog: 'near-optimal memory usage, with a mere waste of under 4%'

examples.claim: Parallel sampling: logical 0,1 of both sequences -> physical 7,1; ref counts both 2
examples.source: paper 4.4: 'mapped to physical blocks 7 and 1 ... reference counts for physical blocks 7 and 1 are both 2'

examples.claim: Beam search k=4: frees blocks 2,4,5,8; all share 0,1,3; candidates 0,1 share 6; 2,3 share 7
examples.source: paper 4.4: 'vLLM frees all physical blocks whose reference counts reach 0 (blocks 2, 4, 5, 8) ... all candidates share blocks 0, 1, 3; candidates 0 and 1 share block 6, and candidates 2 and 3 further share block 7'

examples.claim: Blocks swapped to CPU never exceed total GPU physical blocks; swap space bounded by GPU KV memory
examples.source: paper 4.5: 'the number of blocks swapped to the CPU RAM never exceeds the number of total physical blocks in the GPU RAM'

examples.claim: Swap vs recompute (OPT-13B, ShareGPT): comparable at block size 16-64; recompute overhead never above 20% of swapping latency
examples.source: paper 7.3 / Fig. 19: 'recomputation overhead is never higher than 20% of swapping's latency. For medium block sizes from 16 to 64, the two methods exhibit comparable end-to-end performance'

examples.claim: V1 up to 1.7x throughput vs V0 without multi-step scheduling; Llama 3.1 8B and 3.3 70B on ShareGPT
examples.source: V1 alpha blog: 'up to 1.7x higher throughput compared to V0 (without multi-step scheduling)'; 'Llama 3.1 8B and Llama 3.3 70B models using the ShareGPT dataset'

examples.claim: NVIDIA GPU needs compute capability 7.5+; conda PyTorch statically links NCCL
examples.source: gpu.cuda.inc.md: 'compute capability 7.5 or higher'; 'PyTorch installed via conda will statically link NCCL'

examples.claim: TP rank memory = weight shard + VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE; over a NUMA node -> exitcode 9; legacy, use --kv-cache-memory-bytes
examples.source: cpu.md: 'killed with exitcode 9 due to out-of-memory. This is a legacy setting; use --kv-cache-memory-bytes instead.'

examples.claim: Server applies the chat template stored in the tokenizer by default
examples.source: quickstart.md: 'By default, the server uses a predefined chat template stored in the tokenizer.'

examples.claim: llm.generate returns a list of RequestOutput; generation_config="vllm" restores vLLM defaults
examples.source: quickstart.md: 'returned as a list of RequestOutput objects'; 'set generation_config="vllm" when creating the LLM instance'

examples.claim: --gpu-memory-utilization default: 1.0 with extensible KV cache, else 0.92; per-instance limit
examples.source: vllm/config/cache.py: 'If unspecified, 1.0 with the extensible KV cache ... and 0.92 otherwise'; 'This is a per-instance limit'

examples.claim: KEDA: polls every 15 s, scales up above 5 waiting requests, 1-3 replicas, waits 360 s before scaling down
examples.source: production-stack autoscaling-keda: 'Maintain between 1 and 3 replicas; Scale up when the queue exceeds 5 pending requests; Check metrics every 15 seconds; Wait 360 seconds before scaling down after scaling up'

docs/design/metrics.md and vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py list vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc, vllm:prefix_cache_queries / vllm:prefix_cache_hits (counters), vllm:request_time_per_output_token_seconds and vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds; the three names in the post are not exposed by current vLLM. Post hedges at L645.
